Items.Authors: David Díaz Martín, Alberto Hernández Fernández, Roger John Hoyland, José Alberto Rubiño-Martín, David Hernández Expósito, José Javier Díaz García, Luis Fernando Rodríguez Ramos
Items.Title: Study of RFI from Geostationary and LEO satellite constellations as precursor to QUIJOTE MFI2 Observations
Items.Abstract: As part of the QUIJOTE (Q-U-I JOint TEnerife) Experiment, a Radio Interference Mapper (RIM) has been developed to map signals from geostationary and LEO satellite constellations in the 10.7–12.75 GHz band, and to evaluate their impact on future QUIJOTE MFI2 observations. Since QUIJOTE observes passively outside the ITU RAS protected bands, it must deal with interference from satellites legally operating in these frequencies. While geostationary satellites have been the main challenge so far, the deployment of ~9,000 LEO satellites for Starlink and OneWeb introduces a new and significant source of contamination. RIM uses a commercial 1.0 m offset parabola with an LNC providing four outputs across the band of interest. These four polar signals are injected into four channels of the QUIJOTE MFI2 FPGA-based data acquisition system. The collected data are then processed to quantify and assess the impact of the satellite interference.

Items.Authors: Takumi Ogawa, Masaki Ito, Taro Matsuo, Satoshi Ikari
Items.Title: Study on a new method for acquiring complex visibility using a densified pupil spectroscopy interferometer
Items.Abstract: The formation flying infrared interferometer project, SEIRIOS, will feature an observation instrument called a densified pupil spectroscopy interferometer (DPSI). DPSI relaxes the angular requirements by interfering with two beams of light at the pupil, and by observing each wavelength separately, the requirements for controlling the optical path difference (OPD) are relaxed.  Previously, a method for using DPSI has been considered: splitting the pupil into two and shifting the phase of one half by a quarter wavelength before interfering, thereby simultaneously obtaining the real and imaginary parts of complex visibility. However, there were problems with this method.  We propose a method that can simultaneously obtain the real and imaginary parts of the complex visibility and the spectrum of the target without using a phase plate, by adding an angular error to the light beam. We demonstrate the validity and usefulness of this method using the optical simulator we constructed.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Herrald, Yoko Tanaka, Yosuke Minowa, Mitsuhiro Fukushima, Takeo Fukuda, Masayuki Hoshino, Hikaru Iwashita, Norio Okada, Kenji Mitsui, David Chandler, Hajime Ogane, Yoshito Ono
Items.Title: Subaru Ultimate-GLAO star simulator slice mechanical prototype
Items.Abstract: The Star Simulator is a core component of the Subaru Ultimate-GLAO wave-front sensor alignment and calibration system, consisting of a set of interchangeable light sources and a machined structure to precisely and repeatably locate interchangeable light sources which simulate laser guide stars across the range of altitudes as well as natural guide stars. This paper documents the production and characterisation of a functional prototype (known as the Star Simulator Slice) used to perform individual wave-front sensor alignment, and to validate the manufacturing process for the full system.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Herrald, Darcy Green, Mick Rummery, Les Harris, Mike Bateup, Yosuke Minowa, Noelia Martinez Rey
Items.Title: Subaru ultimate-GLAO wave front sensor de-rotator mechanical prototype
Items.Abstract: The Ground Layer Adaptive Optics (GLAO) system for ULTIMATE is the next-generation instrumentation suite for the Subaru Telescope. The Ultimate-GLAO Wave-Front Sensor (WFS) subsystem includes a set of Laser Guide Star (LGS) and Natural Guide Star (NGS) wave-front sensors, mounted adjacent to the Subaru Cassegrain focal plane. The LGS and NGS wave-front sensor suites are supported at the Subaru Telescope Cassegrain port by a welded and machined steel structure that mechanically interfaces with the Cassegrain derotator of the Subaru Telescope and provides derotation of the LGS WFS. The derotator structures were manufacted by Austec Industrial Engineering Pty Ltd, and inspected, measured and characterised at Mt Stromlo Observatory.

Items.Authors: Katlego Papane, Makubutu Evelyn Nkgadima
Items.Title: System validation of the SKA-Mid signal chain using the ITF Sky Simulator
Items.Abstract: This paper explains the systems engineering approach used to construct the Sky Simulator and integrate it within the broader ITF testbed. We review how to validate interfaces with foreign L2 subsystem providers, confirm L1 performance requirements, and refine operational procedures using hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results reveal that complete sky simulation considerably minimizes integration risk, accelerates commissioning, and boosts confidence in the readiness of next-generation radio telescope infrastructure before deployment.

Items.Authors: Jennifer Ito
Items.Title: Telescope pointing model for POLARBEAR-2b
Items.Abstract: Polarbear-2b (PB-2b) is a cryogenic receiver that was mounted on one of the telescopes in the Simons Array which was situated in the Atacama Desert in Chile at an altitude of 5,200 meters. Each Simons Array telescope was an off-axis Gregorian-Dragone telescope consisting of a 2.5 meter primary mirror and a receiver designed to measure the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB). The work presented here focuses on the pointing model that was developed for PB-2b to characterize the relationship between the telescope encoder readings and its true boresight pointing. We compare multiple pointing models including those used for Simon Array’s predecessor Polarbear, and we determine the best model to use for PB-2b’s science analysis. This work seeks to add to the understanding of systematic errors due to structural dynamics of the telescope in CMB polarization measurements.

Items.Authors: Freddy Munoz Arancibia, Roberto Tighe
Items.Title: Telescope testing with active M1M3/M2 cells: mass balance and dynamics performance during the commissioning of Vera C. Rubin Observatory
Items.Abstract: Description of the mechanical components integration and commissioning of the Simonyi telescope at Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Discussion of the mass budget and balance strategies before first motion, plus dynamic performance results based on high speeds and acceleration requirements. The primary goal is the successful operational start of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time, focusing on image quality and efficiency.

Items.Authors: Matteo Porru, Giorgio Calderone, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Veronica Baldini, Sara Bertocco, Henri Boffin, Roberto Cirami, Igor Coretti, Claudio Cumani, Diego Del Valle, Frédéric Dérie, Mario Kiekebusch, Christophe Moins, Antonio Manescau, Veronica Strazzullo, Antonio Sulich
Items.Title: Template Development in the ELT Software Framework: The FORS Upgrade Project
Items.Abstract: The FORS upgrade project (FORS-Up) is the first real-world deployment of the ELT Instrument Control Software Framework on an operational telescope instrument. As FORS1 is refurbished to replace FORS2 at the VLT, its control software is being fully reimplemented using the new ELT architecture, turning it into a critical proving ground for upcoming ELT instruments.    This paper presents development methodologies drawn from implementing observational procedures for FORS1’s multi-mode operations. We describe a hierarchical template architecture that enforces consistent structure and maximizes code reuse across seven observing modes and several dozen procedures. We provide concrete examples from template code, discuss techniques for reducing overheads through parallel execution, and outline testing strategies using real hardware and high-fidelity simulators. The resulting patterns and lessons learned offer practical guidance for teams developing control software for ELT intruments.

Items.Authors: Benjamin R. Zeiger, Michelangelo von Dassow, Isabella Brown, Danny Herbert
Items.Title: Temporary support structures for x-ray and extreme ultraviolet filters
Items.Abstract: Freestanding thin film transmission filters are an integral part of optics for high energy astrophysics. Sub-micron filter thicknesses typically necessitate mesh or polymer support to survive launch stresses, a design that sacrifices instrument performance for the entire mission life to survive conditions prior to the nominal beginning of life. We present an alternative design incorporating temporary support structures to survive launch conditions, with subsequent removal of the support structure to optimize optical performance.

Items.Authors: Susant Acharya, Langley Payne, Graeme Jonas, Dijana Bogunovic, Andrew Rakich, Barry Adcock, Andrew Cole, Kym Hill, Bryn Emptage
Items.Title: Testing and corrective work on primary mirrors of two 1.2-m class Australian telescopes
Items.Abstract: Kiwistar Optics carried out two major remedial programs for Australian 1.2-m class telescopes: the Great Melbourne Telescope (GMT) primary mirror and the University of Tasmania (UTAS) primary–secondary assembly. The GMT mirror, made from an unconventional fused–borosilicate substrate, showed significant figure errors and orientation-dependent astigmatism with hysteresis. Multi-orientation full-aperture interferometry was used to obtain a stable surface map, and corrective polishing reduced the wavefront error from ~9 waves PV to 0.386 waves PV, making its imaging impact negligible under seeing-limited operation.  The UTAS system presented different challenges: uncertain radii and conic constants in both mirrors produced highly aberrated on-sky images. Double-pass autocollimation and stitched sub-aperture interferometry revealed dominant M1 astigmatism and strong spacing sensitivity, enabling revised optical parameters and clear recommendations for restoring system performance.

Items.Authors: Mattia Maniscalco, Valentina Fioretti, Nicolò Parmiggiani, Andrea Bulgarelli, Gabriele Panebianco, Alessio Aboudan, Luca Castaldini
Items.Title: Testing deep learning techniques for event reconstruction in pair-production gamma-ray telescopes
Items.Abstract: In the development of next-generation tracking detectors for gamma-ray space observations, the integration of advanced deep learning techniques into event reconstruction algorithms is essential for improving the performance of the mission, reducing systematic uncertainties and maximizing the scientific output.   In this study, we investigate the application of deep learning techniques such as Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for the selection, classification and reconstruction of particle tracks resulting from pair production events within the tracker of a conceptual pair-production telescope.   The final goal is improving the angular and energy resolution, as well as computational efficiency, of the telescope, especially in the soft energy range (< 5-10 MeV) where Compton scattering contaminates the tracks reducing the sensitivity in the so-called MeV gap.

Items.Authors: Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Fernando Quirós-Pacheco, Cédric Plantet, Bo Xin, Jordi Molgo, Paulo Henrique Silva, Nicolò Azzaroli, Juan Pablo Haddad, Gary Muller, Alfio Puglisi, Fabio Rossi, Diogo Slepetys, Josema Filgueira, Aline Souza, Dana Adams, Brian McLeod, Jan Kansky, Daniel Catropa, Simone Esposito, Richard Demers
Items.Title: The 2K-actuator deformable mirror and the segmented piston tip-tilt array on the GMT Adaptive optics and Phasing Sensors testbed (GAPS): from calibration to hybrid wavefront control strategies
Items.Abstract: The GAPS testbed is designed to develop and validate the Natural Guide Star Adaptive Optics (NGAO) mode of the Giant Magellan Telescope (GMT). It aims to demonstrate diffraction-limited near-IR performance across the 25.4-m segmented GMT aperture, including operation under poor seeing and with faint guide stars. GAPS integrates the NGWS-P and HCAT platforms with a new GMT-pupil telescope simulator. A 2k-actuator BMC deformable mirror and a segmented SAO Piston-Tip-Tilt array emulate atmospheric turbulence, phasing errors, and their correction. We present calibration results for both devices, introduce the NGAO hybrid wavefront controller for high-order correction and segment-level phasing, and summarize advanced strategies such as stroke minimization and minioning. These developments demonstrate GAPS as a key platform for validating the end-to-end AO and phasing approaches required for GMT first light.

Items.Authors: David A. Del Rizzo, Brent R. Carlson, Alex S. Hill, Charl Baard, Elena Bergeron, Nicholas Bruce, Xuan Du, Andrew D. Gray, Thushara Gunaratne, Mohammad Islam, Dustin Lagoy, Tom Landecker, Robert Messing, Benoit Robert, Ralph Webber, Heng Zhang
Items.Title: The Advanced Radio Telescope Test Array: engineering an upgrade of the seven-element Synthesis Telescope at DRAO
Items.Abstract: The Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory (DRAO) - operated by National Research Council Canada near Penticton, British Columbia, Canada - is home to a seven-element radio interferometer: the Synthesis Telescope (ST). The ST has produced significant astronomical knowledge for Canadian and international radio astronomers for over 50 years, through projects such as the Canadian Galactic Plane Survey, and has been central to a rich history of engineering development at DRAO.    A major signal-path upgrade of the ST is currently underway, engaging the full suite of engineering capabilities within the Radio Astronomy Technology Program at DRAO, from mechanical, digital, analog and software. The Advanced Radio Telescope Test Array (ARTTA) will vastly enhance the science capabilities of the ST, while providing a new, broadband radio interferometer for which a broad range of new technologies can be imagined, designed, prototyped, implemented, and tested on a working telescope system.

Items.Authors: Christiaan D. Brinkerink
Items.Title: The African Millimeter Telescope phase monitor system: low-cost and flexible atmospheric characterisation
Items.Abstract: As part of the development efforts for the African Millimeter Telescope, four simple atmospheric phase monitoring systems, designed in-house at Radboud Radio Lab, have been deployed at multiple sites in Namibia. Each system consists of two COTS satellite dishes connected to a central computer, and measures fluctuations in phase difference from a TV satellite signal in Ku-band. Through these measurements, the stability of the local atmosphere can be monitored and the coherence time of the atmosphere at higher observing frequencies calculated. In this talk, we present the results from these measurements as well as the results from a test campaign to verify the hardware performance, which was carried out in coordination with IRAM at the NOEMA site on Plateau de Bure. We conclude that while our measetup has higher instrumental noise levels than other more advanced (and more expensive) systems, the coherence times calculated using the data from both systems correlates quite well.

Items.Authors: Jonathan Crass, Sai Vidyud Senthil Nathan, Julia Brady, Mark Derwent, Marcelo Tala Pinto, Michael Engelman, Christian Schwab, Julian Stürmer, Jayde Spiegel, Erin Duell, Brian Sands, Daniel Pappalardo, Matheus J. Castro, Justin R. Crepp, Marshall Johnson, Ondrej Kitzler, Thomas Legero, Xavier Lesley, Stanimir Letchev, Jacob Pember, Richard Pogge, Jonathan Shover, Dane Zielinski-Nicolson
Items.Title: The calibration system of the iLocater spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The iLocater spectrograph is a new, near-infrared, extreme precision radial velocity (EPRV) instrument being delivered to the Large Binocular Telescope in 2026. The instrument uses single-mode fibers (SMFs) for light transmission, including for its calibration sources. We present an overview of the iLocater calibration system (including a custom Fabry-Pérot etalon, uranium neon hollow-cathode lamp, halogen source, solar feed, and laser frequency comb) and the strategies adopted to ensure effective injection of calibration light. We also present the custom fiber switching system which is used for efficient distribution of illumination sources to all instrument fibers.

Items.Authors: Mandana Amiri, Charles Bennett, Guinevere Berg, Mark Halpern, Gary Hinshaw, Gordon Lacy, Tom Landecker, Joshua MacEachern, Thomas Rennie, Bruce Veidt, Pedro Villalba-Gonzalez, Janet Weiland, Don Wiebe, Edward Wollack, Parham Zarei
Items.Title: The Canadian Galactic Emission Mapper: a new 8-10 GHz telescope to map the polarization of the northern sky
Items.Abstract: The Canadian Galactic Emission Mapper (CGEM) is a 4-meter single-dish radio telescope located at the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory in Penticton, Canada. CGEM is designed to map polarized galactic synchrotron emission across the entire northern sky from 8 to 10 GHz with 1 MHz frequency resolution. Its goal is to obtain high-fidelity, low-noise maps of polarized galactic synchrotron radiation at frequencies where synchrotron dominates, in order to provide a reliable template for CMB B-mode foreground cleaning. I will show on sky performance of CGEM’s single-pixel azimuthally symmetric telescope and its coherent, dual-polarized radiometer, and show early commissioning data from its first few months of operation.

Items.Authors: Giovanni Lombardi, Sergio Fabiani, Ettore Del Monte, Nicolas De Angelis, Abhay Kumar, on behalf CUSP
Items.Title: The CUSP CubeSat mission for space weather multi-physics analysis, design, and testing
Items.Abstract: The space-based CUbesat Solar Polarimeter (CUSP) mission aims to measure the linear polarization of solar flares in the hard X-ray band by means of a Compton scattering polarimeter. CUSP is a project in the framework of the Alcor Program of the Italian Space Agency aimed at developing new CubeSat missions. We present the outcomes of the CUSP's Phase B study, which is scheduled to end in early July 2026. The design solutions adopted for the mission's most critical multi-physics design drivers will be discussed, these solutions have been formulated and applied to demonstrate compliance with system requirements at both the spacecraft and platform levels. We describe the mechanical design of each structural component, the results of finite element analyses and topological optimization of the interface between the platform and payload. Moreover, we will discuss the validation of the Payload model based on the environmental testing campaign (e.g., vibration) carried out on a demonstrator.

Items.Authors: Matthew Whiting, Matt Austin, Aidan Hotan, Minh Huynh, Vanessa Moss, Wasim Raja
Items.Title: The data processing and archiving workflow for the ASKAP telescope
Items.Abstract: The ASKAP Telescope is a cm-band synthesis imaging radio telescope operated by CSIRO at Inyarrimanha Ilgari Bundara, the CSIRO Murchison Radio-astronomy Observatory in Western Australia. Its defining feature is its wide field-of-view, made possible by the innovative phased-array-feed (PAF) receivers. This field-of-view results in very large data rates, that require prompt supercomputer-based processing to ensure continual survey observing is possible.    This presentation will detail the autonomous workflows that allow us to take the 4 TB/hr data rate and produce science-ready products that are made available through CASDA, ASKAP’s archive. It will cover the constraints generated by prompt processing, and how the compute environment has shaped the design of the different subsystems and the event-based messaging framework that enables the orchestration. The presentation will also cover lessons learned, with experience from the first three years of full survey operations.

Items.Authors: Ronald A. Lopez, Crystal Kim, Benjamin Mazin, John I. Bailey
Items.Title: The design and integration of the optical system for MOMOS: multi-object MKID optical spectrometer
Items.Abstract: Conventional high-resolution echelle spectrometers are optimized to obtain detailed spectra over a limited field of view, typically through a single slit or fiber. In contrast, multi-object spectrometers (MOSs) are built to image spectra from many targets at once. However, this capability often comes with trade-offs in spectral resolution, wavelength coverage, and instrument complexity. Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) present a solution to this challenge, due to their photon counting capability and inherent energy resolution. MKIDs can be used to dramatically simplify the optical design of a MOS while attaining the high resolution of an echelle spectrometer. MOMOS realizes this concept and lays the foundation for a new class of spectrometers that do not need to compromise resolution or coverage. We present the design and performance of the MOMOS optical system, including an overview of its optical layout, alignment strategy, and the resulting image and spectral quality.

Items.Authors: Rico Landman, Sebastiaan Haffert, Louis Desdoigts, Matthijs Mars, Adam Taras, Elena Tonucci, Yinzi Xin
Items.Title: The Dutch extreme adaptive optics testbed: goals and opto-mechanical design
Items.Abstract: We report on the goals, design, and ongoing development of the Dutch Extreme Adaptive Optics (XAO) testbed currently under construction in Leiden. It aims to develop and validate innovative technologies and algorithms to push the limits of high-contrast imaging on the upcoming Extremely Large Telescopes (ELTs). The testbed is fully reflective and is designed to operate at visible and near-infrared wavelengths. It consists of an XAO module with the possibility for multiple deformable mirrors and a suite of wavefront sensors. It also includes a coronagraphic arm that facilitates common coronagraph architectures and dark hole digging. We will present the opto-mechanical design of the testbed, detailing the key trade-offs considered to achieve deep contrasts. We will also show end-to-end simulations of the testbed and its predicted performance.

Items.Authors: Eduardo A. Bendek, Enrico Biancalani, Edward Balaban, Rachel Ticknor
Items.Title: The FLUTE 1 technology demonstration mission and payload
Items.Abstract: The Fluidic Telescope (FLUTE) concept enables large-aperture space observatories, overcoming scaling limitations of segmented mirrors by using thin liquid films that naturally form smooth spherical mirrors in microgravity. The ultimate goal is a 50-meter class observatory. We report on the conceptual design for FLUTE-1, a 1-meter aperture technology demonstration mission designed for Low Earth Orbit. The paper presents the conceptual design for the spherical aberrations corrector and the core instrumentation: a Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor to characterize the fluidic mirror's optical performance, and an imaging camera to obtain the first images and assess imaging performance. FLUTE-1 is a crucial step toward validating fluidic optics for large-scale space astronomy.

Items.Authors: Mauro Centrone, Marco Faccini, Ivan Agostinelli, Lorenzo Paonni, Alessando Di Filippo
Items.Title: The INAF–OAR laser guide stars for adaptive optics laboratory: a new national facility for advance LGS-AO systems
Items.Abstract: We present the new INAF LGS–AO Laboratory, a national facility established to strengthen Italy’s capabilities in advanced adaptive optics (AO) and Laser Guide Star (LGS) technologies. Funded through the Italian Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), the laboratory provides a fully equipped environment for end-to-end Assembly, Integration, and Verification (AIV) of AO subsystems. Its infrastructure includes high-power laser systems, precision wavefront sensors, deformable mirrors, interferometric diagnostics, turbulence simulators, and real-time control hardware, enabling development, testing, and innovation in AO, LGS, and AI-driven wavefront control. The facility also supports research in laser ranging, optical communication, and space-debris monitoring, serving as a national hub for optical technologies.

Items.Authors: Gerardo Capobianco, Jeffrey S. Newmark, Yeon-Han Kim, Davide Loreggia, Marta Casti, Hervé Haudemand, Donguk Song, Sung-Hong Park, Su-Chan Bong, Kyungsuk Cho, Seonghwan Choi, Qian Gong, Ji-Hye Baek, Jongyeob Park, Jihun Kim, Heesu Yang, Nelson L. Reginald, Nicholeen M. Viall, Silvano Fineschi, Federico Landini, Luca Zangrilli, Lucia Abbo, Jason Budinoff
Items.Title: The in-flight radiometric calibration of the COronal Diagnostic EXperiment (CODEX)
Items.Abstract: The Coronal Diagnostic Experiment (CODEX), a solar coronagraph developed by NASA-Goddard Space Flight Center in collaboration with the Korea Astronomy and Space Science Institute (KASI) and the Italian National Institute for Astrophysics (INAF), was successfully operational on-board the International Space Station (ISS) from December 2024 to September 2025. During its nine months of operation, CODEX executed four dedicated radiometric campaigns. These campaigns were crucial for performing in-flight radiometric calibrations, a fundamental step required to convert the measured raw data (counts) into meaningful physical units. The calibration was achieved by repeatedly targeting a select number of bright stars within the instrument’s pointing range, for which well-characterized spectra were available. This presentation describes and analyzes the dataset, methodology, and results of this essential radiometric calibration effort

Items.Authors: Rosario Cosentino, Luca Di Fabrizio, Guillermo González de Rivera, Álvaro Quintana, Marcos Hernández Díaz, Luis Riverol Rodríguez, Hector Ventura, Manuel D. Gonzalez, Carmen Vélez, Kashif Buland, Juan Antonio Leñero Bardallo, Sergio López Buedo, Ángel Rodríguez-Vázquez, Enrique Pérez, Ester Amou Loumagne, Robert Content, Adriano Ghedina, Francisco Prada
Items.Title: The La Palma Quantum Interferometer (LPQI): cryogenic SPAD camera head, thermal validation, and first timing tests
Items.Abstract: We present the latest developments of the LPQI SPAD sensor module, designed as a compact, thermally stabilized platform integrating the SPAD array, the readout FPGA, and the cooling system on a single PCB. A dedicated cryogenic chamber was characterized using the operational detector board, validating the Peltier-based thermal architecture with stable −20 °C operation and <±0.1 °C fluctuations under simulated 0–3 W loads. In parallel, the FPGA acquisition chain demonstrated reliable handling of asynchronous SPAD events, fine timestamping, and sub-nanosecond synchronization when disciplined by a White Rabbit clock. These results confirm the readiness of the integrated module for the upcoming electro-optical tests, including photon detection efficiency, dark count rate, and full timing performance.

Items.Authors: Kevin Gilliam, Chad F. Bender, Gilberto Chavez Lopez, Warren B. Foster, Riley Mikkelsen, Brian Scaramella, Richard Wortley, Andy Monson
Items.Title: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope: a scalable ROS-2 based architecture for distributed telescope control
Items.Abstract: The LFAST project is building a 20-cell telescope array to provide large collecting area at lower cost than traditional single apertures. Each cell includes auxiliary imaging for alignment and wavefront sensing, a primary mirror with three degrees of freedom, and a thermally actuated figure-control system using 24 regulated TEC elements. Scaling to 20 cells creates a very large number of controllable degrees of freedom. Coordinating them as one instrument presents challenges in distributed control, synchronization, device-health monitoring, and fault isolation. LFAST uses open-source astronomy software and ROS 2 for modular development, component reuse, and real-time array coordination. This paper presents the control architecture and lessons learned from building a scalable, cost-effective system for independently actuated telescope cells.

Items.Authors: William Thompson, Chad Bender, Richard Wortley, Jason Patrou, Peter Gray, Kevin Gilliam, Gilberto Chavez Lopez, Trevor Dugan, David Zeller
Items.Title: The Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope: Rev 1.5 design modifications
Items.Abstract: This paper describes design and development improvements for the Large Fiber Array Spectroscopic Telescope (LFAST) mechanical structure and drive systems. LFAST is an innovative concept that aims to provide a large collecting area for astronomical spectroscopy at low cost by mass producing large numbers of inexpensive 0.76m unit telescopes.

Items.Authors: Lucio Angelo Antonelli
Items.Title: The Large Size Telescope (LST) for the south observing site of CTAO
Items.Abstract: The LST-South project is aimed at construct and operate two complete Large-Sized Telescopes (LSTs) at the southern site of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). The approved and fully funded program commenced on January 1, 2023, with a completion deadline of April 30, 2026. The mechanical structure’s baseline design is derived from that of existing northern LSTs, but with important modifications to meet the environmental requirements of the southern site. The mirrors are produced using a technology developed in Italy by the Italian National Institute of Astrophysics (INAF) through a cold replica of glass slabs to fabricate the large mirrors. The cameras are developed under the responsibility of INFN virtually identical to those of LST North. The production of cameras, mirrors, and mechanical structures has been accomplished through substantial industrial contracts that are overseen by project management. This presentation is aimed at presenting the overall project

Items.Authors: Sander ter Veen, Jan David Mol, Boudewijn Hut
Items.Title: The LOFAR telescope manager: a second-generation system to fully manage a telescope
Items.Abstract: If you want to do a great job, you need to do it twice! We are fortunate that we have that chance while building a new software infrastructure to operate LOFAR2, the successor of the Low Frequency Array that operated for 10 years as the worlds largest low frequency radio telescope. In this contribution, we will give an overview of the LOFAR Telescope Manager, the sub-system that manages the telescope processes of specification, scheduling, telescope and pipeline control, storing metrics, logs, managing dataproducts, and deployment of the various services. We will present how it interacts with the other systems like the telescopes, the central processing clusters, and the monitoring and maintenance systems and we will highlight choices made based on past experiences and current technology.

Items.Authors: Ana I. Gómez de Castro, Juan Larruquert, Maria Frutos, Ada Canet, Paloma López-Reyes, Carlos Miravet
Items.Title: The Lunar Ultraviolet Observatory OUL: optical design and scientific trade-off analysis
Items.Abstract: The Lunar Ultraviolet Observatory (OUL – Observatorio Ultravioleta Lunar) is the scientific payload selected by the Spanish Space Agency for an upcoming lunar mission. Its primary objective is to observe the Earth's exosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. However, due to its design and orbital configuration, OUL will also serve as a UV monitor of the heliosphere and the Galaxy. Its wide field of view and operational range (115–175 nm) make OUL a particularly demanding optical instrument. Before initiating the breadboarding of the optics, a detailed trade-off analysis between reflective and transmissive band-selection approaches has been conducted, including laboratory tests and numerical simulations. The results of this study will be presented in this communication.

Items.Authors: Wim Pessemier, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Wim De Meester, Wannes Verstraeten, Maddalena Reggiani, Kwinten Missiaen, Bart Vandenbussche, Hans Van Winckel, Mario Kiekebusch, Dan Popovic, António Amorim, Jean-Christophe Barrière, Thomas Bertram, Peter Bizenberger, Emilie Bouzerand, Olivier Corpace, Yigit Dallilar, Martin Kulas, Dirk Lesman, Jeff Lynn, Lars Mohr, Vianak Naranjo, Philip Parr-Burman, Chad Salo, Silvia Scheithauer, Benoît Serra, Roy van Boekel, Shiang-Yu Wang
Items.Title: The METIS instrument control system during system AIV
Items.Abstract: METIS, the Mid-Infrared ELT Imager and Spectrograph, has entered its Assembly, Integration, and Verification (AIV) phase in Europe, starting in late 2025 with the installation of the cryostat at the Integration Facility in Leiden, the Netherlands. Automated Instrument Control System (ICS) procedures such as evacuation, cooldown and warmup were already in place at that time thanks to an early deployment strategy that uses final electronics and software already at subsystem level, to validate critical parts of the system at consortium member locations prior to system integration in Leiden. The paper presents the current ICS status, and its role in validating the emerging system and subsystem development. We further discuss how the ICS addresses the complexities of this distributed AIV phase, while highlighting some technical challenges encountered so far.

Items.Authors: Nicolas Levraud, Eric Gendron, Caroline Kulcsár, Nicolas Galland, Henri-François Raynaud, Yann Clénet, Richard Davies
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: first on-bench performance tests of the SCAO hybrid LQG+Integrator controller
Items.Abstract: The Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) is expected to begin scientific operations in 2030, with MICADO as its first-light imager. The Single Conjugate Adaptive Optics (SCAO) system for MICADO is currently being assembled and tested at the Observatoire de Paris.    We present the first experimental results of MICADO’s baseline AO control strategy that uses a hybrid approach: a Linear Quadratic Gaussian regulator for low-order modes, optimized to adapt to the disturbance caused by vibrations and ELT windshake, and an integral action controller for higher-order modes.

Items.Authors: Ulf Brauneck, Gunnar Garnier, Ester Aranzana, Joost van den Born, Annemieke Janssen
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: first results of medium and broadband NIR filters
Items.Abstract: We present the first results of a set of 21 different types of medium and broadband NIR interference bandpass filters manufactured by SCHOTT Suisse S.A., Switzerland for the ELT’s first light instrument MICADO developed by NOVA optical infrared instrumentation group at ASTRON. The filters covering wavelengths from 800 to 2500 nanometers target the specific Astronomical NIR-band I, Y, J, H and K along with subbands within these ranges. The Infrasil fused silica substrates were also manufactured at SCHOTT Suisse S.A. and the coatings where applied with plasma assisted reactive magnetron sputtering technology allowing a highly stable, uniform and precise coating method. Real-time optical monitoring ensures each layer reaches its exact thickness, enabling the creation of complex, high-performance interference filters. We present the first results of measurements performed on the manufactured filters during the ongoing production.

Items.Authors: Andreas Emslander, Florian Lang, Lenard Spallek, Federico Biondi, Kateryna Kravchenko, Fabio Waldhör, Heinrich Huber, Michael Krzyzowski, Ilja Aul, Marcel Bornstein, Eckhard Sturm, Richard Davies, Sebastian Rabien
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: manufacturing progress of the MICADO cryostat and lessons learned regarding the mechanical design
Items.Abstract: MICADO, the Multi-AO Imaging Camera for Deep Observation, will be one of the first light instruments for the 39m Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory (ESO) in Chile on the Cerro Armazones mountain.   The continuous LN2 flow cryostat, which will operate at 82 K, is the centerpiece of the instrument, housing all major cold subsystems such as the cold optics, mechanisms with filters and masks, and the detectors. This paper outlines the cryostat manufacturing process and highlights the main insights gained about its mechanical design. We also describe the assembly of the large vacuum vessel and of the cold bench components after the welding and milling process at the manufacturing company.

Items.Authors: Elsa Huby, Pierre Baudoz, Gauri Padalkar, Fabrice Vidal, Nicolas Levraud, Yann Clénet, Richard Davies
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: tuning STARLOC, the star tracking algorithm for the MICADO Lyot coronagraphs
Items.Abstract: The ELT/MICADO instrument will include three classical Lyot coronagraphs with different occulting spot sizes to optimize high-contrast observations in the J, H, and K bands. However, stellar image drifts are expected during observations, which can significantly degrade coronagraphic performance. We have developed the STARLOC (Star Tracking Algorithm for Regular Lyot Occulting Coronagraph) to estimate and correct the centering error of the stellar image on the occulting spot, aiming for stabilization within 0.5 mas. The algorithm relies on cross-correlation between the coronagraphic image and a well-centered reference. We present the optimization of key parameters and the simulated performance of STARLOC in the presence of static aberrations, AO residuals, and detector noise, as well as on the experimental validation.

Items.Authors: Alan Vasquez Soto, Nicholas Law, Glenn Walters, Mike Ronco, Hank Corbett, Jonathan Carney, James Dockery, Megan Dubay, Shannon Fitton, Lawrence Machia, William Marshall, Thomas Procter, Donovan Schlekat, Alex Bucheli
Items.Title: The mount structure for the Argus Array: design, analysis, and testing
Items.Abstract: The Argus Array, an 8m-class telescope, will monitor 8,000 square degrees with 1,200 individual 28-cm telescopes from a single facility. Following evaluation of multiple prototypes, we developed a novel mount structure for Argus. Through iterative refinement, we created a structure designed to meet performance requirements within budget constraints. The beam-and-tube framework achieves <1 arcsecond pointing drift over 3-degree tracking ratchets with <0.35 arcseconds RMS tracking error. The mount interfaces with the Conic Drive tracking platform through a pin-and-roller configuration, implementing load distribution and isolation that prevents drive deformations from propagating to telescope mounting points. Flexure simulations have been validated through tilt sensor measurements and independent external analysis. We present mechanical implementation, fabrication specifications, simulation validation, interface assembly procedures, and structural testing outcomes.

Items.Authors: Arie Blumenzweig
Items.Title: The Multiple Aperture Spectroscopic Telescope (MAST)
Items.Abstract: The Multiple Aperture Spectroscopic Telescope (MAST) employs a scalable control system that coordinates many small telescope units for multi-object spectroscopy. Each telescope unit acquires, tracksand guides feeding light through optical fibers to centralized spectrographs, while a FastAPI-based controller manages synchronized, safe operation. The architecture uses MongoDB for configuration, capability-based permissions, WebSocket notifications, and integrated weather and resource monitoring. Observation plans and tasks are defined in TOML and validated with Pydantic. System roles are distributed across Windows IoT devices that control individual telescopes, a Windows machine that manages the spectrographs, and a Linux controller responsible for planning, scheduling, safety supervision, and science operations. Items.Authors: Veronica Baldini, Roberto Cirami, Giorgio Calderone, Igor Coretti, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Antonio Sulich, Kamal Sant, Ilaria Ermolli
Items.Title: The new control system for IBIS 2.0: upgrading a solar imaging spectropolarimeter from the Dunn Solar Telescope to THEMIS
Items.Abstract: The Interferometric BIdimensional Spectrometer (IBIS) has been a key instrument for high-resolution imaging spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry at the Dunn Solar Telescope (DST, NSO, USA). As part of its relocation and upgrade to the THEMIS solar telescope (Tenerife, Spain), the instrument — now IBIS 2.0 — has undergone a complete redesign of its control electronics and software.  The new architecture is based on industrial Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) distributed across two dedicated control cabinets mounted near the instrument. This modular and robust configuration ensures precise coordination of all opto-mechanical subsystems, including the dual Fabry–Pérot interferometers, the polarization modulation unit, and the imaging cameras. The PLCs provide deterministic timing, precise motion control, and continuous status monitoring, while interfacing with high-level control software based on ESO VLT standards within the THEMIS observatory environment.

Items.Authors: Germano Bianchi, Pietro Bolli, Federica Caputo, Franco Fiocchi, Matteo Fiorentini, Francesco Fiori, Giacomo Lorenzo, Jacopo Malagoli, Sergio Mariotti, Michele Martelli, Andrea Mattana, Giovanni Naldi, Manuela Naldi, Andrea Orlati, Federico Perini, Alessandro Poli, Nicola Ragno, Emanuele Santandrea, Marco Schiaffino, Michela Zardi
Items.Title: The new life of the Northern Cross radio telescope: Revolutionizing space surveillance and the FRBs hunt
Items.Abstract: The Northern Cross radio telescope, one of the world's largest with a 30,000 square meters area, has undergone a major PNRR-funded renovation to address critical astronomical challenges like detecting transients and Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs), alongside monitoring satellites and space debris. The upgrade focused on the 564-meter-long East-West arm, significantly increasing its field of view from 2° to 28°. This was achieved by installing 480 new Yagi-Uda antennas connected to an adaptive beamforming system, allowing efficient tracking of radio sources and satellites. A new data center with high-performance computing enables dual-use applications: precise FRB research and enhanced space debris monitoring. This technological advancement positions the Northern Cross as a key sensor for the European Space Surveillance and Tracking (EU-SST) network and promises to deliver unprecedented progress in understanding FRBs and the evolution of the Universe through milli-arcsecond-level localization

Items.Authors: Davide Ricci, Andrea La Camera, Marcello Ravenna, Laura Schreiber, Emiliano Diolaiti, Giuliana Fiorentino, Carmela Lardo, Claudia Mignone, Maria Tantalo, Antonino Nunnari, Vittorio Francesco Braga
Items.Title: The new Starfinder for PSF modeling and image analysis: a free software in Python with a web user interface
Items.Abstract: We present the Python release of the Starfinder crowded-field photometry/astrometry package for images with complex, spatially variable PSFs, especially from adaptive optics.     The new GUI is a client application based on web technologies, while the core routines retain the proven empirical-PSF methodology with performance/functional upgrades. New optimizations target very large images and extended PSF models, enabling efficient analysis of future ELT-scale datasets.     The code is released as open access with documentation and tutorials and can be simply installed as a python package.

Items.Authors: Samantha Gray, Ranjani Srinivasan, Gabriel Dubinsky, Manuel Fernandez, Rurik Primiani, Ryan Chaves, Lindy Blackburn, Rick Raffanti
Items.Title: The ngBackend: an ultra-wideband signal processing system for the Event Horizon Telescope
Items.Abstract: The current R2DBE samples two 2 GHz baseband channels at 4.096 Gsps and requantizes them to 2‑bit VDIF streams for 10 GbE transport, but system performance remains constrained by sampler bandwidth, limiting achievable sensitivity and array scalability.The next‑generation back end addresses these limitations through two new subsystems: a block downconverter (BDC) incorporating a novel up/down‑conversion architecture, and a digital backend (DBE) sampling at 16.384 Gsps, digitizing a contiguous bandwidth of 8.192 GHz before re-quantizing down to 2 bits and outputting VDIF data at 128 Gbps nominally. This system enables ultra‑wideband operation, providing approximately 32 GHz of aggregate data from a single ngDBE. This paper describes the overall ngBackend system design and laboratory performance, with emphasis on the BDC architecture and design and the characterization and testing of the wide‑input‑bandwidth Adsantec ADCs used for digitization.

Items.Authors: Arijit Maiti, Mudit K. Srivastava, Vipin Kumar, Bhavesh Kumar Mistry, Ankita Patel, Vaibhav Dixit, Ruchi Pandey, Jay Chitroda
Items.Title: The on-sky performance and first science results of ProtoPol: a medium resolution echelle spectro-polarimeter for PRL telescopes
Items.Abstract: ProtoPol is a medium-resolution echelle spectro-polarimeter developed for the PRL 1.2m and 2.5m telescopes at Mt Abu observatory, India. Developed completely with commercially available off-the-shelf components, ProtoPol was designed on the concept of echelle and cross-disperser gratings covering a wavelength range from 4000-9600 angstrom with spectral resolution in the range of 0.4-0.75 angstrom. A dedicated, fully automated echelle spectro-polarimetric data reduction pipeline was developed for echelle spectro-polarimetric/spectroscopic data analysis. A sample of Herbig Ae/Be stars, classical Herbig stars, Symbiotic stars, and AGB/post-AGB stars were observed as a part of ProtoPol’s science verification program. In this proposed talk, the speaker shall discuss the on-sky characterization and performance verification of ProtoPol, the data reduction pipeline development for echelle spectro-polarimetric/spectroscopic data reduction, and present its first science results.

Items.Authors: Antonio Sulich, Gino Tosti, Veronica Baldini, Igor Coretti, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Giovanni Pareschi, Salvatore Scuderi
Items.Title: The PLC's software architecture for ASTRI Mini-Array
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI project (Astrofisica con Specchi a Tecnologia Replicante Italiana) led by INAF (Italian National Institute of Astrophysics) was created to study astronomical sources that emit gamma rays at very high energies. The ASTRI Mini-Array project entails building and installing nine Cherenkov telescopes at the Teide Observatory in Spain, with seven units already completed. This document focuses on the development of the local control software of the telescopes, developed on a Beckhoff PLC using the TwinCAT environment.

Items.Authors: Richard Deno Stelter, Cyril Bourgenot, Andrew Skemer, Renate Kupke, Paul White, James T. Wells, Spencer Davies, Lee Bainbridge, David Bramall, Daren Dillon, Cristian A. Rodriguez, Nicholas K. Mac Donald
Items.Title: The SCALES slenslit: motivation, opto-mechanical design, and performance
Items.Abstract: SCALES (the Slicer Combined with Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) is a thermal infrared, lenslet-based IFS (integral field spectrograph) designed to work at the diffraction limit of the Keck II telescope. Like all IFSs, there is a tradeoff made among plate scale, field of view, instantaneous spectral resolution, and spectral separation. However, we have designed a unique hybrid IFS that uses a slicer to reorganize the discontinuous field of view generated by the lenslet array into a pseudoslit suitable for mid-resolution spectroscopy, trading field of view for spectral resolution. This has several advantages opto-mechanically, and broadens the scientific grasp of SCALES considerably. The slicer optics (including three-mirror anastigmat input and output relays) were fabricated by the Centre for Advanced Instrumentation at the University of Durham, England. We discuss the design and fabrication of the SCALES slenslit and present on its performance.

Items.Authors: Heiko Salzmann, CTAO-US/SCT collaboration
Items.Title: The Schwarzschild-Couder Telescope for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory: latest improvements to the optical system
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is a future ground-based observatory for gamma-ray astronomy providing unparalleled sensitivity in the energy range from 20 GeV up to 300 TeV. Three telescope types with differently sized reflectors are foreseen. The Schwarzschild-Couder telescope (SCT) is a dual mirror design proposed for the medium energy range of 100 GeV up to 10 TeV. A complex system facilitates the alignment of the two segmented mirrors consisting of 48 and 24 mirror panels for the primary and secondary mirror, respectively. The performance of the optical system was verified with the prototype SCT (pSCT) installed at the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory in southern Arizona, USA. Currently on-going efforts involve the upgrade of the alignment system of the pSCT. This contribution presents the latest improvements to the optical system, along with the latest performance estimates for the instrument based on simulations.

Items.Authors: Yuta Miki
Items.Title: The Simons Observatory: development of a cryogenic lens mount with reduced mechanical lens stress in the small aperture telescopes
Items.Abstract: The Simons Observatory (SO) aims to detect the primordial B-mode polarization of the CMB to constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio. SO has begun observations with three small aperture telescopes (SATs) located on the high-altitude Atacama Plateau in Chile. Each telescope employs silicon lenses held by lens mounts within the cryogenic optics tube cooled to 1 K. However, during pre-deployment tests, several lenses cracked due to a design flaw in the lens mounts. To address this, we developed a modified lens mount to mitigate the risk. This presentation reports on the failure investigation, performance evaluation and installation of the new lens mounts into SATs.

Items.Authors: Paulo Simões, Tiago Giorgetti, Guillermo Giménez de Castro, Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, Amauri Kudaka, Gabriel F. Silva, Ian Grinkraut, Guilherme Cavazzana
Items.Title: The solar ultraviolet to near-infrared spectrometer (SUNS)
Items.Abstract: We present the Solar Ultraviolet to Near-infrared Spectrometer (SUNS), a new ground-based telescope–spectrograph system dedicated to visible and near-infrared spectroscopy of solar white-light flares. SUNS is being developed to provide temporally resolved, well-calibrated spectra of active regions and flares across the visible band, with extensions toward the ultraviolet and near-infrared. We will describe the instrument concept, observing modes, and expected performance, and discuss how SUNS will help discriminate between competing emission mechanisms for the flare in the visible continuum.

Items.Authors: Berke V. Ricketti, Victoria Yankelevich, Ettore Pedretti, Andy Vick, Evelina Zubyte, Giorgio Savini, Locke Spencer, Gerard van Belle, Lee Mundy, David T. Leisawitz
Items.Title: The SPace-based InterFerometer Feasibility (SPIFF) Project: finding a path towards a technology demonstration mission for space-based interferometry in times of limited funding
Items.Abstract: Space-based interferometry promises transformational angular resolution, yet no direct-detection synthetic-aperture interferometer has flown. Technical complexity, low system-level TRL, and community scepticism have stalled progress despite strong scientific demand. The SPIFF Project is a UK-led, internationally partnered effort to define a coherent, stepwise path toward a future space interferometer mission. SPIFF will build on UK strategic priorities, industrial capabilities, and recent progress on a thermal-IR spatio-spectral interferometer breadboard. A central element is an international consortium, including PIs from previous mission concepts, to capture lessons learned and avoid repeating past challenges. By uniting technology development, community engagement, and heritage expertise, SPIFF aims to deliver a credible roadmap for future space interferometry and inform the landscape ahead of the U.S. Astro2030 and ESA long-term planning cycles.

Items.Authors: Mikhail Sachkov, Evgeniy A. Kopylov
Items.Title: The Spektr-UF mission: status 2026
Items.Abstract: A general description of the project “Spektr-UF” (Spectrum-UV, World Space Observatory - Ultraviolet) aimed at creating a large space observatory for operation in the UV wavelengths (115 - 310 nm) is given.   Spectr-UF – is a multipurpose space observatory equipped with a telescope of 170 cm primary mirror diameter. The main task of the observatory is obtaining high-resolution spectra of cosmic objects and images of diffraction quality in the UV region (115–310 nm).  Hear we briefly describes the current status of the project, focusing on some new touches. The scientific program of the project has been clarified, a new project of the field camera has been prepared; more optimal orbit has been selected; a system for collecting applications has been developed and experimental collection of applications has begun.

Items.Authors: Ivan Di Antonio, Simone Lombardi
Items.Title: Thermal compensation in the Einstein Telescope: a preliminary study
Items.Abstract: Thermal gradients in the mirrors of current and next-generation gravitational wave interferometers cause optical aberrations that can significantly affect their stability and sensitivity. In the future Einstein Telescope (ET) high-frequency arm, the high expected circulating power will induce a significant optical path difference in the Fabry-Perot cavity, which would compromise the functionality of the interferometer unless properly compensated. In this paper the induced thermal aberrations (thermo-elastic and thermo-optic contributions) are assessed, both analytically and through finite-elements analyses. Actuation patterns are then introduced in the analyses, properly modeled in shape and magnitude to restore the nominal RoC of the mirrors and to minimize the optical path difference, thus compensating for the undesired thermal effects. Preliminary requirements for the future Thermal Compensation System of ET are finally presented.

Items.Authors: Philipp Huke, Viljon Sekseni, Kersten Mumme, Freerk Schütt, Dhruti Mavani, Tobias Brunken, Mohamed Shehata, Miriam Brandt
Items.Title: Three-port Fourier-transform spectrometer for high precision differential measurements
Items.Abstract: To get a high resolution with a Fourier-transform Spectrometer (FTS) long paths are needed, even though a few cm already suffice to exceed resolutions of most echelle spectrographs. This allows to build compact FTS for monitoring calibration sources with high precision and accuracy when calibrated properly. The slow speed of the moving mirror(s) require a sophisticated detector-architecture. Especially for broad-band or incoherent sources strong averaging is needed to compensate for the small SNR outside the coherence length.  Here, we report about a FTS with three input-ports. Three input-ports allows to measure two ports in a differential mode, thereby using the third port for reference. This is particularly useful to measure differentially the behaviour of fibers. The detector architecture is based on fast, low-noise photodiodes with low amplification and a conventional ADC. The six output ports enhance the SNR and enable relatively fast measurement of broad-band light sources.
